name: Customers Served
definition: The number of connected customer accounts (metered service points) supplied with electricity during the reporting period, expressed as a count of customers. It counts active connections or billing accounts, not the number of people, and is sliced by customer type, service area and provider via the dimension columns rather than by name. This count is the denominator for per-customer benchmarks and for the SAIDI/SAIFI reliability indices, so count connections consistently and do not confuse it with population served.

name: Total Planned Interruptions Customers Affected
definition: The total number of customer-interruptions caused by planned (scheduled and pre-notified) supply interruptions in the reporting period, expressed as a count of customers. Each interruption event contributes the number of customers it disconnected, and these are summed across events, so a customer affected by two separate planned outages is counted twice. Momentary interruptions (typically under one minute) are excluded by convention. This is a numerator feeding the planned component of SAIFI; it counts customer-interruptions, not unique customers.

name: Total Unplanned Interruptions Customers Affected
definition: The total number of customer-interruptions caused by unplanned (forced or unscheduled) supply interruptions in the reporting period, expressed as a count of customers. Each event contributes the customers it disconnected and these are summed, so a customer hit by several faults is counted once per event. Momentary interruptions (typically under one minute) are excluded by convention. This is a numerator feeding the unplanned component of SAIFI; it counts customer-interruptions, not unique customers.

name: Planned Downtime Events
definition: The count of planned (scheduled) outage events during which a generating unit or network element was taken out of service in the reporting period, expressed as a number of events. Planned downtime covers scheduled maintenance, inspections and overhauls arranged in advance, as distinct from forced outages. It measures asset availability at the equipment or plant level and is sliced by asset, utility function and provider via the dimension columns.

name: Unplanned Downtime Events
definition: The count of unplanned (forced or unscheduled) outage events during which a generating unit or network element was unavailable in the reporting period, expressed as a number of events. Unplanned downtime covers breakdowns, trips and fault-driven shutdowns not scheduled in advance. It measures asset reliability at the equipment or plant level and is sliced by asset, utility function and provider via the dimension columns.

name: Total Planned Interruptions Events
definition: The count of distinct planned (scheduled and pre-notified) supply interruption events affecting customers during the reporting period, expressed as a number of events. Unlike downtime events, which describe an asset being out of service, an interruption event is one that disconnects customer supply. Momentary interruptions (typically under one minute) are excluded by convention. This count supports the planned component of SAIFI and network reliability reporting.

name: Total Unplanned Interruptions Events
definition: The count of distinct unplanned (forced or unscheduled) supply interruption events affecting customers during the reporting period, expressed as a number of events. It captures fault-driven and other unscheduled interruptions to customer supply, as distinct from asset downtime. Momentary interruptions (typically under one minute) are excluded by convention. This count supports the unplanned component of SAIFI and network reliability reporting.

name: Hours in Period
definition: The number of calendar hours in the reporting period, expressed in hours. For a full year this is 8,760 hours, or 8,784 in a leap year, and proportionally fewer for a month or quarter. It serves as the time denominator for availability, capacity factor, load factor and similar time-normalised calculations. Enter the actual hours for the specific period being reported rather than assuming a standard year.

name: Planned Downtime Hours
definition: The cumulative duration for which a generating unit or network element was out of service for planned (scheduled) reasons during the reporting period, expressed in hours. It sums the hours of scheduled maintenance, inspection and overhaul outages and, together with Hours in Period, drives availability and utilisation metrics. Measured at the equipment or plant level and sliced by asset and utility function via the dimension columns.

name: Unplanned Downtime Hours
definition: The cumulative duration for which a generating unit or network element was unavailable for unplanned (forced) reasons during the reporting period, expressed in hours. It sums the hours lost to breakdowns, trips and fault-driven shutdowns and, together with Hours in Period, drives reliability and forced-outage metrics. Measured at the equipment or plant level and sliced by asset and utility function via the dimension columns.

name: Solar Hours of Irradiance (H_irradiance)
definition: The number of hours of usable solar irradiance received at a solar array during the reporting period, expressed in hours (conceptually equivalent to peak sun hours). Here "Solar" denotes the physical measurement domain, not a dimension slice: it is an environmental input variable recorded per array at equipment level. It is used with measured and reference irradiance and rated capacity to assess theoretical yield and performance ratio, so it describes sunlight availability rather than any electrical output.

name: Network Length
definition: The total circuit length of transmission and/or distribution lines in the network, expressed in kilometres. It measures the physical extent of the wires network and is sliced by voltage level, line type (overhead versus underground) and service area via the dimension columns rather than being split into separate measures. Used as a denominator for network density, loss and reliability indicators; confirm whether route-km or circuit-km is intended when comparing utilities.

name: Fuel Oil
definition: The volume of fuel oil consumed by a generating unit during the reporting period, expressed in litres. It captures the liquid fuel burned to produce electricity (for example diesel or heavy fuel oil) and is recorded per generating unit at equipment level, sliced by fuel type and provider via the dimension columns. Used with generation to derive fuel efficiency and specific fuel consumption; keep it distinct from lubrication oil.

name: Lubrication Oil
definition: The volume of lubricating oil consumed by a generating unit during the reporting period, expressed in litres. It captures lube oil used and topped up in engine operation, recorded per generating unit at equipment level and sliced by asset and provider via the dimension columns. It is a maintenance and operating-cost input and should not be combined with fuel oil, which is the combustion fuel.

name: Total Planned Interruptions Customer Minutes
definition: The total customer-minutes lost to planned (scheduled and pre-notified) supply interruptions in the reporting period, being the sum over all affected customers of the duration each was without supply, expressed in customer-minutes. Each event contributes its customers-affected multiplied by its restoration duration, and these are summed across events. Momentary interruptions (typically under one minute) are excluded by convention. This is the numerator feeding the planned component of SAIDI.

name: Total Unplanned Interruptions Customer Minutes
definition: The total customer-minutes lost to unplanned (forced or unscheduled) supply interruptions in the reporting period, being the sum over all affected customers of the duration each was without supply, expressed in customer-minutes. Each event contributes its customers-affected multiplied by its restoration duration, summed across events. Momentary interruptions (typically under one minute) are excluded by convention. This is the numerator feeding the unplanned component of SAIDI.

name: Distribution Transformer Rated Capacity
definition: The nameplate apparent-power rating of distribution transformers, expressed in MVA. It is the installed capacity the transformers are designed to carry continuously, recorded at the service-area level and sliced by asset, voltage and service area via the dimension columns. Used with average load to assess transformer utilisation and headroom; it is a capacity (MVA) figure, not an energy (MWh) flow.

name: Distribution Transformer Average Load
definition: The average apparent-power loading carried by distribution transformers over the reporting period, expressed in MVA. It represents the mean demand on the transformer fleet and, when compared with rated capacity, indicates utilisation and spare capacity. Recorded at the service-area level and sliced by asset and service area via the dimension columns; do not confuse average load with peak load.

name: Rated Capacity
definition: The nameplate (installed) real-power capacity of a generating unit, expressed in MW. It is the manufacturer-rated continuous output of the unit and is recorded per unit at equipment level, sliced by energy source and provider via the dimension columns rather than defined per fuel. PRISM aggregates unit ratings up to station, service-area and utility totals; be clear whether gross nameplate or net (derated) capacity is being entered, and keep MW capacity distinct from MWh energy.

name: Electricity Sold to Customers
definition: The metered electrical energy billed to customers during the reporting period, expressed in MWh. It is the revenue-generating energy that reaches customer meters, sliced by customer type, tariff and service area via the dimension columns. Together with energy sent out it defines system losses (energy sent out less energy sold), and with non-revenue energy it reconciles total delivered energy; confirm units are MWh, not kWh, when entering.

name: Non-Revenue Energy Consumed
definition: The electrical energy that entered the system but was not billed to customers during the reporting period, expressed in MWh. It comprises technical losses (in lines and transformers), commercial losses (theft, metering error, unbilled use) and any unmetered own consumption, sliced by loss type and service area via the dimension columns. It is the difference between energy delivered into the network and Electricity Sold to Customers, and underlies the non-revenue-energy / system-loss percentage; enter in MWh and avoid double-counting station auxiliaries.

name: Electricity Generated
definition: The gross electrical energy produced by a generating unit during the reporting period, measured at the unit's terminals before deduction of station auxiliary consumption, expressed in MWh. It is a single measure sliced by energy source and provider via the dimension columns, not a separate measure per fuel, and is recorded per unit at equipment level. Because this is gross generation, net energy sent out equals generation less station auxiliary usage; confirm gross-versus-net and MWh-versus-kWh conventions when entering.

name: Energy Stored
definition: The electrical energy taken into an energy storage system (for example a battery) during the reporting period, expressed in MWh, recorded per storage unit at equipment level. It represents energy absorbed into storage and is sliced by asset and provider via the dimension columns. Distinguish it from Electricity for Charging (energy drawn to charge) and Electricity Discharged (energy delivered back out); round-trip efficiency means stored and discharged energy differ.

name: Electricity Discharged
definition: The electrical energy delivered out of an energy storage system during the reporting period, expressed in MWh, recorded per storage unit at equipment level. It is the energy the storage system returns to the network or load and is sliced by asset and provider via the dimension columns. Because of round-trip losses it is less than the energy taken in to charge; keep it separate from Electricity for Charging (input) and Energy Stored.

name: Electricity Demand Average Load
definition: The average electrical demand placed on the system over the reporting period, expressed in MWh as the mean load, recorded at the service-area level. It represents the typical loading of the system rather than its extremes and is sliced by service area and provider via the dimension columns. Used with peak load to derive load factor; do not confuse average load with peak load or with total energy sent out.

name: Electricity Demand Peak Load
definition: The maximum electrical demand placed on the system during the reporting period, expressed in MWh as the peak load, recorded at the service-area level. It is the highest instantaneous or interval demand reached and is sliced by service area and provider via the dimension columns. Peak load sizes capacity requirements and, with average load, gives load factor; keep it distinct from average load and installed capacity.

name: Station Auxilliary Usage
definition: The electrical energy consumed by a power station's own auxiliary equipment during the reporting period, expressed in MWh, recorded at the power-station level. It covers in-house loads such as pumps, fans, control systems and lighting that the station uses to operate, sliced by station and provider via the dimension columns. It is the difference between gross generation and net energy sent to grid, so include it when reconciling gross and net energy and avoid counting it as customer or network loss.

name: Electricity Purchased from Other Providers
definition: The metered electrical energy bought from other generators or providers (for example independent power producers) during the reporting period, expressed in MWh, recorded at the service-area level. It is energy the utility takes onto its system from third parties and is sliced by provider and energy source via the dimension columns. It adds to own generation in the supply balance; keep it distinct from own generation and from energy sold to customers.

name: Electricity Sent to Grid
definition: The net electrical energy delivered into the grid during the reporting period, expressed in MWh, recorded at the service-area level. It equals gross generation less station auxiliary usage (energy sent out) and is sliced by provider and service area via the dimension columns. Together with energy sold and non-revenue energy it forms the supply-and-loss balance; because it is net of auxiliaries, do not equate it with gross Electricity Generated.

name: Lost Time Frequency Multiplier
definition: The standardising constant used to scale lost-time injury frequency to a common exposure base, expressed as a ratio (dimensionless). It is the multiplier (commonly 1,000,000 or 200,000 hours worked, depending on the convention) applied when computing the Lost Time Injury Frequency Rate so that utilities of different sizes are comparable. Record the multiplier consistent with the reporting standard in use; it is a calculation constant, not a count of injuries.

name: Solar Electricity Generated Theoretical
definition: The theoretical (expected) electrical energy a solar installation should have generated during the reporting period given the measured solar resource and the array's rated capacity, expressed in kWh, recorded per array at equipment level. Here "Solar" is the physical domain of the measure, not a dimension slice. It is derived from irradiance, sun hours and rated capacity and is compared with actual output to compute performance ratio and identify underperformance; it is a modelled reference value, not metered generation.

name: Electricity for Charging
definition: The electrical energy drawn to charge an energy storage system during the reporting period, expressed in kWh, recorded per storage unit at equipment level. It is the energy consumed at the input to charge the battery, sliced by asset and provider via the dimension columns. Because of charging and round-trip losses it exceeds the energy later discharged; keep it distinct from Energy Stored (energy absorbed) and Electricity Discharged (energy delivered out).

name: Solar Average measured irradiance (G_measured)
definition: The average solar irradiance actually measured at the plane of a solar array during the reporting period, expressed in W/m2, recorded per array at equipment level. Here "Solar" denotes the physical measurement domain rather than a dimension slice; it is an environmental input from a pyranometer or reference cell. It is compared with the standard test condition irradiance to normalise and assess array performance, so it describes incident sunlight intensity, not electrical output.

name: Solar Standard Test Condition irradiance (G_STC)
definition: The reference solar irradiance at Standard Test Conditions used to rate photovoltaic modules, expressed in W/m2 (conventionally 1,000 W/m2), recorded per array at equipment level. Here "Solar" denotes the physical measurement domain rather than a dimension slice. It is the fixed benchmark against which measured irradiance is normalised when calculating expected yield and performance ratio, so it is a reference constant rather than a field measurement.
